_comment: Tier-2 corpus for the document-store STORAGE PRIMITIVE (writeDatabaseDocument /
linkDocumentContent / ensureLinkFolderId). Both v4 and the Rust port run the same
write sequence against the same mount-index fixture and the resulting four tables
(doc_mount_files, doc_mount_documents, doc_mount_file_links, doc_mount_folders) are
structural-diffed in the minted-values REMAP form (ids minted internally, timestamps
minted internally → first-seen id-token remap across all four tables + timestamp
placeholders). The store row (doc_mount_points) is seeded with a pinned id so every
write's mountPointId is identical on both sides (NOT remapped).
SAFETY: testPepperBase64 is a THROWAWAY 32-byte key, the same one every other
tier-2 fixture uses; it decrypts nothing real.
Scenarios: (1) a top-level JSON file → permissive policy; (2) a top-level markdown
file with no frontmatter → permissive; (3) a markdown file in a subfolder → exercises
ensureLinkFolderId creating the Knowledge folder; (4) a second path with content
byte-identical to (2) → dedup-by-sha (reuses one file + one document row, new link);
(5) rewriting path (2) with new content → link upsert-in-place + a new file/document
row (the old ones survive, still referenced by (4)); (6) a markdown file whose
frontmatter sets character_read:false → the policy cascade forces all three allow*
flags to 0, verified against v4's real yaml-based policyFromContent;
(7) [0a0419f5] KNOWLEDGE/atlas.md — a case-variant of the existing Knowledge folder:
ensureLinkFolderId REUSES it under its stored casing, so the link's relativePath is
Knowledge/atlas.md (canonical dir) and NO KNOWLEDGE folder row is minted;
(8) [0a0419f5] DESCRIPTION.md — a case-variant of the existing description.md link:
the NOCASE upsert updates that row IN PLACE keeping its description.md casing (new
file/document, the link's relativePath/fileName unchanged).
[40319484] Deliberate hard-link groups. doc_mount_blobs joins the dump (a sixth
table) so the blob leg's payload GC is measured, not reasoned about. New op kinds:
'bind-group' drives the REAL bindLinkGroup over two links resolved by path, and
'delete' drives the REAL deleteDatabaseDocument (deleteWithGC).
(9-10) twins/left.md + twins/right.md written with byte-identical content → one
content row, two links, the twins folder minted; (11) bind-group left↔right mints a
linkGroupId on BOTH; (12) rewriting left.md with frontmatter character_read:false →
fanOutGroupFileId repoints right.md AND carries plainTextLength + conversionStatus +
all three allow* flags (so right.md goes 0/0/0 without being written), the now-
unreferenced first content row is collected WITH its document payload, and
reindexLinkGroupSiblings rebuilds right.md's per-linkId chunk set;
(13) twins/third.md dedups onto left's new content row, ungrouped; (14) bind-group
left↔third EXTENDS the existing group (same id, left's row untouched) rather than
minting a second one; (15) rewriting THIRD.md — a non-anchor member, and a case
variant — fans out to both siblings and carries the permissive flags back.
The twins group is deliberately never unlinked, so all three members keep real
paths and the v4 sibling-re-chunk divergence stays nameable by path (see the
differential's CHUNK_DIVERGENCES).
(16-22) the pair/ group is the delete arm, and is deliberately NOT written after
binding (so no sibling re-chunk is involved): three members bound into one group,
then deleting two.md leaves 2 survivors → the group id stays, and deleting three.md
leaves 1 → 'a group of one is not a link', so one.md's linkGroupId is NULLed. Each
delete also collects its now-unreferenced content row + document payload.
(23-24) solo.md written then rewritten with NO group and NO other reference →
the ordinary ungrouped rewrite-GC (the case every instance hits on every edit,
and the leak this commit fixes);
(25-28) logo.bin + logo-copy.bin via linkBlobContent with identical bytes but
DIFFERENT descriptions/extracted text → one content row, two links; then bind-group;
then rewriting logo.bin with new bytes → the blob fan-out's textState-null asymmetry:
logo-copy.bin follows the fileId but KEEPS its own description and extractedText, and
the abandoned content row is collected along with its doc_mount_blobs payload.
